Why This Is Asked
- Tests cross-cluster policy propagation, conflict handling, and secure identity management
- Validates runtime enforcement by per-tenant sidecars in a multi-cluster CNF gateway mesh
- Probes reconciliation loops and secure communication patterns

Key Concepts
- CustomResourceDefinition for TenantPolicy
- Cross-cluster replication with mTLS and SPIFFE IDs
- Dynamic gateway policy loading in sidecars
- Conflict resolution and eventual consistency

Code Example
```yaml
# CRD: TenantPolicy
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantpolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID:
                type: string
              namespaces:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
              rules:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    action:
                      type: string
                      enum: [allow, deny]
                    resources:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: tenantpolicies
    singular: tenantpolicy
    kind: TenantPolicy
```

```yaml
# Policy Agent Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: policy-agent
  namespace: cnf-system
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: policy-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: policy-agent
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: agent
        image: policy-agent:latest
        env:
        - name: REMOTE_CLUSTER
          value: "peer-cluster.example.com"
        - name: SPIFFE_TRUST_DOMAIN
          value: "example.com"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: spiffe-bundle
          mountPath: /run/spiffe
      volumes:
      - name: spiffe-bundle
        configMap:
          name: spiffe-bundle
```

```yaml
# Test Namespace Manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: TenantPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-policy
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenantID: tenant-a
  namespaces:
  - tenant-a
  rules:
  - action: allow
    resources:
    - service-a
    - service-b
```

## Why This Is Asked

```yaml

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-rollout
spec:
  replicas: 2
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: cnf
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates understanding of tenant isolation, mTLS, and certificate rotation using cert-manager in a CNF (Cloud-Native Function) gateway context. It also assesses practical knowledge of in-cluster secret management and sidecar integration patterns.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Secrets and per-tenant namespace isolation
- Mutual TLS termination in a gateway sidecar
- cert-manager Issuers and automatic certificate rotation
- Tenant identity extraction from X.509 certificates

## Code Example
```yaml
# Per-tenant CA Issuer
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca-cert
---
# Certificate with auto-rotation
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-server-tls
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  secretName: tenant-<id>-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  duration: 168h
  renewBefore: 72h
  dnsNames:
    - gateway.tenant-namespace.svc.cluster.local
  subject:
    organizations:
      - tenant-<id>
---
# Gateway Deployment with mTLS sidecar
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-namespace
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
      - name: mtls-sidecar
        image: mtls-proxy:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 9443
        env:
        - name: TENANT_CA_PATH
          value: /etc/certs/ca.crt
        - name: VALIDATE_CLIENT_CERTS
          value: "true"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
        - name: tenant-ca
          mountPath: /etc/certs
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: tenant-<id>-tls
      - name: tenant-ca
        secret:
          secretName: tenant-ca-cert
```

## Validation One-Namespace Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-001
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-cert
  namespace: tenant-001
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-encoded-ca-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-encoded-ca-key>
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: tenant-001
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca-cert
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-001-tls
  namespace: tenant-001
spec:
  secretName: tenant-001-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  duration: 168h
  renewBefore: 72h
  dnsNames:
    - gateway.tenant-001.svc.cluster.local
  subject:
    organizations:
      - tenant-001
```

## Key Implementation Details
1. **Certificate Rotation**: cert-manager automatically renews certificates before expiration using the `renewBefore` field
2. **Tenant Isolation**: Each tenant has isolated namespaces, CAs, and TLS secrets
3. **mTLS Validation**: The sidecar validates client certificates against the tenant-specific CA
4. **Tenant ID Extraction**: The tenant ID is extracted from the certificate subject (organization field) to enforce access policies

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to design dynamic per-tenant feature flags, integrate a Wasm-based runtime gate, and outline a minimal Kubernetes manifest plus the data-path logic.

## Key Concepts

- Envoy Wasm / WASM filters
- Kubernetes CustomResourceDefinition (CRD)
- Deterministic per-tenant rollout using hash-based selection
- Observability: metrics, tracing, and rollback strategies

## Code Example

```rust
// Minimal pseudo-logic for Wasm gate
fn should_allow(tenant: &str, flag: &str, rollout: u8) -> bool {
  let seed = hash(tenant + ":" + flag) % 100;
  seed < rollout as u32
}
```

```yaml
# CRD (TenantFlag)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantflags.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: tenantflags
    singular: tenantflag
    kind: TenantFlag
```

```yaml
# TenantFlag instance (test-namespace)
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: TenantFlag
metadata:
  name: adobe-featureX
  namespace: test-namespace
spec:
  tenantID: adobe
  flagName: featureX
  rolloutPercent: 25
  enabled: true
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you validate rollout accuracy across tenants and detect drift?
- What rollback and monitoring would you implement if a flag causes regressions?
